supporting_evidence: Existing stack identity rules require identical definition, owner, location, charges, durability, equipment state, and metadata before merging.
Partial transfer operations already split atomically and require a deterministic post-transfer destination state.
Projected maximum_stack metadata provides an evidence-gated capacity boundary without inventing Classic limits.
assumptions: Only explicitly stackable definitions can merge.
Destination stacks are filled in stable instance-ID order because native selection order remains unresolved.
Overflow remains a separate valid stack instead of being discarded or rejected.
safe_fallback: Do not merge non-stackable or non-identical instances; reject malformed maximum_stack metadata during validation; retain overflow as its transferred instance.
runtime_impact: Bank, merchant, inventory, container, and generic quantity transfers reconcile compatible destination stacks atomically.
character_save_impact: Fully absorbed transferred identities are removed; surviving destination and overflow identities persist with validated quantities.
world_state_impact: Merchant, bank, container, and room-owned stack quantities remain normalized without exceeding projected limits.
native_dependencies: Native overflow messaging and transaction behavior
